description: Tuning governing-rules set (#2108) on real, published text: requirements quoted from the OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 (authentication, sessions, authorization, data protection, logging), against requirements quoted from real openemr/openemr GitHub issues that governing-03 does not use. Labelled blind to every prompt of the product by two AI labellers other than the agent that chose the requirements, with a third pass on each disagreement. Iterate prompts here for real policy text; governing-03 stays held out.
license: Policy text: quoted from the OWASP ASVS 5.0.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 (OWASP Foundation); policy-v1.md stays under CC BY-SA 4.0. Requirement text: short excerpts quoted from public openemr/openemr GitHub issues, each with its URL (items[].source). Labels, summaries and annotation: CC0-1.0.

policy.title: Web Application Security Requirements: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 (excerpts)

annotation.labelledBy: two independent AI labellers (claude-opus-5-5), blind to every prompt of the product and neither of them the agent that chose the requirements, adjudicated by a third pass; not a person
annotation.procedure: Policy quoted from the OWASP ASVS 5.0.0; requirements quoted from real OpenEMR issues by the agent dispatched on #2108, which wrote no label. Labelled against policy-v1 by two tool-less sessions given only the policy and the requirements; each disagreement settled by a third tool-less pass with a written reason. No arm had run on it when the labels were fixed. See ANNOTATION.md and labelling/. #2140 added OS-26 to OS-33, chosen and quoted by the agent dispatched on #2140, which wrote no label, and labelled the same way (labelling/2140/) before any arm ran on them; then ran governing-03's per-rule consistency pass on PA-04, PA-10 and AZ-01 over all 33 items, after arms had run on this set, changing a cell only where both blind passes agreed.

rules.summary: User-set passwords are at least 8 characters; 15 is strongly recommended.
Users can change their own password.
Changing a password asks for the current and the new password.
New or changed passwords are checked against at least the 3000 most common passwords.
No password composition rules: any characters allowed, no required character types.
Password fields are masked; showing the password temporarily is allowed.
Pasting, browser password helpers and password managers are allowed.
No periodic password rotation; a password stays valid until compromised or changed.
Controls against credential stuffing and password brute force are in place.
Access to the application needs multi-factor authentication.
Users are notified after their authentication details change.
System-generated initial passwords are random, follow the policy, expire, and cannot stay as the long-term password.
Resetting a forgotten password is secure and does not bypass multi-factor authentication.
Administrators can start a user's password reset but cannot choose the user's password.
With a separate identity provider, the application checks the authentication strength the provider reports.
A new session token is issued at sign-in and re-authentication, and the old one ended.
An inactivity timeout forces re-authentication.
A logged-out or expired session cannot be used again; the server invalidates it.
After a password or factor change, the user can end all other sessions.
Every signed-in page has an easy, visible way to log out.
Session lifetime and termination between the application and an identity provider behave as documented.
Each function is open only to users with explicit permission for it.
Each data item is open only to users with explicit permission for it.
Authorization is enforced on the server, not by client-side controls.
Sensitive data such as tokens goes in the request body or headers, never in the URL.
Each log entry records when, where, who and what.
Every authentication attempt, successful or not, is logged.
Failed authorization attempts are logged.
Logged data is encoded to prevent log injection.
Logs are protected from unauthorized access and cannot be modified.

items.title: logout doesn't return to login screen after session times out
items.text: so user has to have a bookmark of login screen or have a home page set to login page … not sure if the logic flow makes it to this code

items.title: Password is not obscured when resetting user password
items.text: When resetting a user password, "User`s New Password" is not obscured in the way that it is for "Your Password". The password is successfully obscured when creating a new user, this is only an issue when resetting a user's password.

items.title: Logout from expired session
items.text: … To reproduce, let session expire or get closed. Then try to use 'Logout' dropdown option from menu. Noticed that logout.php does get called but user gets no response possibly because changes to auth library resulting in login.php never getting called. This was a decent compromise to users having to enter emr link in address bar.

items.title: Single sign on
items.text: For a big part of the user of the system used, we need to add the SSO on Openemr to recognize and authenticate the user when the user logged on to the account or laptop the user used. … Is it possible to support any kind of SSO like SAML2 to Openemr?!

applies.businessFact: Will the SSO identity provider enforce multi-factor authentication for every user before granting OpenEMR access?
Does the EHR need a specific authentication strength, method or recentness from the IdP (for example MFA for clinicians), and must it check this in the IdP response?
What is the maximum time allowed between IdP authentication events before the EHR forces re-authentication, and should logging out of one end the session in the other?

items.title: Fix portal generate random password does not return password
items.text: The last commit with the patient access onsite refactor in create_portallogin.php was generating an empty password sent out because the function did not return the password. Not sure how I missed that, lol, but going to fix it ASAP.

applies.businessFact: Are generated portal passwords produced with a cryptographically secure random generator, and do they expire or have to be changed at first login?

items.title: login_fail_counter not reset when an admin resets a password
items.text: When you reset a user's password in Admin-> Users … There is nothing that will reset the login_fail_counter in users_secure. Right now, you have to manually go into the table and reset the field to 0 for a user to log in again if you have max reties enabled and admin reset a password.

applies.businessFact: Does the security documentation require the failed-login counter to be cleared when an administrator resets a user's password?

items.title: Language selection on portal login screen does not match username and password structure
items.text: When allowing a language selection, the label is full width and text centered with the select box below it. This differs from the above username and password setup where the labels are flush left, next to the input selection. Language choice should continue the design pattern

items.title: Remove Password Composition Requirements
items.text: Currently, passwords are required to have a number, lowercase letter, uppercase letter, and special character. However, many security standards, such as NIST (section 5.1.1.1) and ASVS (standard 2.1.9) recommend against password composition requirements because they do not significantly increase the strength of passwords. … Do not require passwords to contain numbers, special characters, etc.

applies.businessFact: Will passwords set or changed under the new policy be rejected if they appear in a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords that meet the policy?

items.title: Show/Hide password button is not present on the login page.
items.text: The show/hide password button is not present on the login page as required by ASVS control ID: 2.1.2 …

items.title: feat: Password strength meter missing
items.text: According to ASVS 2.1.8 there should be a password strength meter provided to help users set a stronger password which is missing in the application. This may be a security threat. … According to the ASVS, when a user is setting their password, a password strength meter should be provided.

items.title: feat: Notify users for password issues
items.text: Users may not know that their password have expired or failed for login attempts. … Add a notification email to system email queue so user can fix any upcoming issues.

applies.businessFact: Are passwords configured to expire on a fixed schedule, or only when a password is found to be compromised?

items.title: bug: Calendar: user created appointment is invisible due to duration of zero minutes
items.text: A user created an appointment. The appointment is not visible to the user in the calendar, thus not clickable, due to a duration of zero minutes. (The duration of zero minutes happened because of a custom category, but was not the user's intention.) … Expected behavior: That the appointment would have some minimum height, thus be clickable.

items.title: password administration logging
items.text: Add detailed password administration logging

applies.businessFact: What must each password administration log entry record (for example the acting admin, target user, action, timestamp and source IP)?

items.title: Patient Portal Logout - Not Working
items.text: The Patient Portal logout functionality is currently not working as expected. When a user attempts to log out, instead of being redirected to the login page, the system displays a "Requested URL not found" error. Its reproduced in the live demo server also.

applies.businessFact: Does a portal logout invalidate the session on the server even when the redirect fails?

items.title: Token expire shows error instead of login screen
items.text: When the authentication token expires, the user is not logged out. Instead, the portal displays an error indicating that the site ID is missing. This is misleading, as the actual issue is an expired authentication token rather than a missing site parameter. … Expected behavior: The user should be logged out automatically and redirected to the login screen when the token expires. A clear message such as "Session expired. Please log in again." should be shown instead of a site id missing error.

items.title: CSRF token exposed in URL in interface/patient_file/letter.php back-link
items.text: The CSRF token is embedded directly in the URL query string (csrf_token_form=...). Because the app enforces CSRF validation on GET requests via CsrfUtils::checkCsrfInput(INPUT_GET, ...), this pattern is encouraged across the codebase. CWE-598. Tokens in URLs leak via: Referer headers when the page loads external resources or the user follows outbound links. Browser history, bookmarks, screenshots. Reverse proxies, web-server access logs, APM/analytics tooling.

items.title: Upgrade entry points (acl_upgrade.php, sql_upgrade.php) allow unauthenticated HTTP access
items.text: acl_upgrade.php and sql_upgrade.php both declare $ignoreAuth = true before loading interface/globals.php, which skips auth.inc.php. Anyone who can reach these scripts over HTTP can invoke them, potentially triggering ACL/schema mutations without any authenticated session. … These scripts are reachable from the admin UI (admin.php) mid-upgrade, and historically had to run before any user account exists.

applies.businessFact: Must these upgrade scripts stay reachable before any user account exists, or can they be gated behind authenticated (MFA) admin access?
Must acl_upgrade.php and sql_upgrade.php still run before any user account exists, or can they be restricted to authenticated administrators (or a one-time setup token)?

items.title: Honor X-Forwarded-For only from trusted proxies in audit logging
items.text: collectIpAddresses() (library/sanitize.inc.php:29) appends $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR'] to the logged IP string with no check that the request actually arrived through a trusted reverse proxy. The returned ip_string is then written into the log table by EventAuditLogger::newEvent() for login events, MFA failures, API requests (src/Common/Logging/Audit/LogTablesSink.php), and other auth events. Any client that can reach the OpenEMR HTTP listener directly … can set X-Forwarded-For to arbitrary text and have it persisted verbatim in the audit trail. … Structured logging. Return remote_ip and forwarded_for as separate fields and persist them as separate columns / structured payload in the audit log rather than concatenating into the comments string.

applies.businessFact: Must forwarded_for values be validated as IP addresses (or encoded) before they are written to the audit log?

items.title: feat(portal): add multi-factor authentication to patient portal
items.text: The OpenEMR patient portal has no multi-factor authentication. Patient login is username/password with optional reCAPTCHA only. There is no TOTP, U2F, WebAuthn, magic-link, SMS, or email-OTP option for patients, and no admin toggle to require any second factor. … This proposes adding MFA to the portal from scratch: TOTP at minimum, with a portal_force_mfa global mirroring the practitioner-side enforcement work, plus a self-enrollment page under portal/account/.

applies.businessFact: Will portal_force_mfa be enabled so that every patient must use a second factor to access the portal?
Must the patient portal's forgotten-password reset require the patient's enrolled MFA factor before a new password can be set?

items.title: Add Prescription History to Patient Report
items.text: Add Prescription History as an option to the Patient Report, as this information can be important to have available and share. … Add option for "Prescription History" to the patient report. If there are no prescriptions, then the report would display "No prescriptions on file". If there are prescriptions on the patient chart and the options is checked, then the report would display all the prescription entries and be available to print/download as PDF.

applies.businessFact: Should the Prescription History report option be available only to users holding an explicit prescription/medication view permission?

items.title: reactor(audit): Improve immutability and tamper-resistance
items.text: Today, the event logging system uses encryption as a means of trying to address certification requirements around immutability and tamper-resistance. The logic is well-intentioned, but somewhat faulty. … Proposal stages: Remove encryption from the audit logs (on all columns that use it). … Update table permissions: log (and log_comment_encrypt) should have permissions set at a MySQL level to allow INSERT and SELECT, but not UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, etc. Ideally, the "default" openemr DB user has no access to the table(s) at all; a new user with minimum permissions should exist for dedicated access. Have some sort of checksum chaining, similar to how git commit hashes work. Tamper detection could examine the chain, re-checksum, and ensure there are no mismatches

applies.businessFact: Will the default openemr database user be denied all access to the log tables, leaving only a dedicated least-privilege account?

items.title: [ACL] Users with only "Patients → Demographics (Write)" permission are unable to edit patient demographics
items.text: A user assigned only the Patients → Demographics (Write) permission through Advanced ACL is unable to edit patient demographic information. Although the user can access the Demographics page, all fields remain in read-only mode and cannot be modified. … Expected Result: The user should be able to edit patient demographic fields and save the changes based on the assigned Write permission.

items.title: bug/The calendar needs to scale horizontally
items.text: In the Calendar day view, when many providers are selected, provider columns are squeezed into the available viewport width instead of expanding and scrolling horizontally. That makes provider names hard to read, the provider close (X) control hard to use, and appointment cells too narrow to work with comfortably. … Expected behavior: Each provider column keeps a usable minimum width so names and controls remain readable/clickable. When providers exceed the viewport width, the calendar grid scrolls horizontally.

items.title: Admin unblock UI parity for new MFA and portal-account lockout counters (… followup)
items.text: … added three new failed-login counter axes for brute-force throttling: per-user MFA, per-IP MFA, per-portal-account. Each of these can auto-recover via the corresponding window (default 3600s = 1h), but if an admin disables auto-recovery (window=0) OR wants to unblock a legitimate user faster than the window, they currently have no UI. … This issue tracks parity: extend the existing surfaces to cover the new MFA counters, and add a small new report for the per-portal-account counter … Shipping a lockout mechanism without a corresponding admin recovery UI is a self-DoS risk.

applies.businessFact: Does the security documentation allow administrators to clear MFA and portal-account lockout counters manually before the lockout window ends?
Which ACL permission is required to use the unblock function for the new lockout counters?

items.title: bug(documents): DICOM viewer shows only the first image of a zip and fails when the images differ in size
items.text: When a zip of DICOM images is opened in the Documents DICOM viewer, only the first image is shown, and if the images have different sizes (for example a landscape and two portrait views of one study) the viewer also raises "A load error has occurred. See log for details." and the other images are lost. … Expected behavior: Every image in the zip can be viewed, one at a time (previous/next), each fitted to the viewer, whatever its size.

items.title: Strengthen part of username and password creation process
items.text: This file is called when a user begins setting up OpenEMR for the first time … Make the following happen via HTML5 attributes: initial user password min length of 12. database password min length of 12. Also: the "initial user" of "admin" is too easy to guess … make the username a minimum of 12 characters as well to ensure if they don't go with our randomized suggestion they still pick something with some complexity (enforce with html5)

applies.businessFact: Is the initial user password entered during setup checked against a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords that meet the 12-character policy?

items.title: Force new user change default password in first login
items.text: How can I force all new users change default password in first login? If applicable to define security steps to users?! for Example: Need all users in first login do the following: 1. Change default password. 2. force to have TOTP step

applies.businessFact: Will the new password chosen at the forced first-login change be checked against a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords?
Are new users' default passwords securely randomly generated for each user, and do they expire after a short period if not used?

items.title: 5.0.2 Bug: Portal asks to create new username when changing pass when email only is on
items.text: The patient portal in 5.0.2 asks for the user to create a new username when they are changing passwords when email substitution for usernames is turned on. This shouldn't be happening when this is turned on.

applies.businessFact: Does the portal password change form require the patient's current password as well as the new password?

items.title: Telehealth Third Party Onetime Login Link invitations both copy link and email
items.text: Building on the one time login links that Jerry built, we want to have the third party participants be able to get a one time invitation as well. We also want to be able to copy the invitation link and invitation message for the third party. Since we generate these links on the fly we need a button to be able to generate the link and copy it since browsers prevent direct copy access when doing an asynchronous request.

applies.businessFact: Are third-party one-time login tokens securely randomly generated, and do they expire after a short period as well as after first use?
Which users or roles are explicitly permitted to generate and send third-party telehealth invitation links?

items.title: feat: Add ability to prevent forced portal credential change
items.text: Currently we force patient to change their credentials when portal credentials are created from MRD. Some admins prefer to prevent this action. … Add and persist a checkbox flag to create_portallogin to set the patient_access_onsite portal_pwd_status column to prevent. A nice addition while here would be to create a onetime to auto login and take patient to say portal documents to create intake forms or to appointments or even the portals change password dialog.

applies.businessFact: Will the one-time auto-login token be passed in the URL or query string, or only in the message body or headers?

items.title: feat: When google single sign on is enabled it still requires user to use password from openEMR to sign the encounter doesn't use single sign on.
items.text: Even with google single sign on it still requires user to use password from openEMR while signing the encounter. Google single sign on works perfectly with the login but when it comes to signing an encounter single sign on doesn't work. It requires openEMR user password. We have made it where it will use single sign for encounter signing. …

applies.businessFact: When an encounter is signed via Google SSO, does the application require and verify a fresh authentication (for example auth_time or forced re-prompt) from the information Google returns?

items.title: feat: Improve Portal Credential Settings page for patients
items.text: Clinican testing of the patient portal credential settings page found the page to be confusing. They recommended changing up some of labels, providing more visual separating for the various credential settings and making the username and password updates independent of each other.

applies.businessFact: Will the independent password update on the portal credential settings page require the patient's current password as well as the new one?
Will the redesigned portal password update reject passwords found in a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords?
Is the patient notified, for example by email, after their portal username or password is changed?
After a portal password change, is the patient given the option to terminate all other active sessions?

items.title: [Patient Dashboard] Credentials reset dialog displays an outdated read-only email address after the patient's email is updated
items.text: A patient exists with Patient Portal credentials. … 1. Login as Administartor. 1. Create a patient. 2. Generate Patient Portal login credentials. 3. Update the patient's email address in the patient record. 4. Save the changes. 5. Click Reset option under Credentials … Actual Result: The Credential reset dialog displays the previous email address in a read-only field. Since the field is not editable, the administrator cannot update it before sending the reset. Expected Result: The password reset dialog should display the current email address from the patient's record. If the patient's email has been updated, the reset dialog should reflect the updated value instead of a stale email address.

applies.businessFact: Does the admin-initiated portal credential reset send the patient a reset link or a system-generated secret that the administrator never sees or chooses?
